description:
Programme Overview

Computer science research at The University of Manchester builds on a legacy that includes the world's first stored-program computer, spanning major advances in AI and advanced computing systems. As a postgraduate researcher, you will work within the Department of Computer Science, based in the Kilburn Building, on research addressing global challenges from the foundations and technologies of computer science to enabling responsible AI and using big data for societal benefit.

Research Areas

The Department of Computer Science is one of the largest in the UK covering a huge spectrum of Computer Science topics. Current areas of expertise range from Neuromorphic Systems to Systems and Software Security. Core Computer Science research is augmented by interdisciplinary research taking place at the interface with discipline areas including mathematics, physics, medicine, biology, and engineering.

Programme Details

  • Duration: 3-4 years full-time or equivalent part-time
  • Qualification: Doctor of Philosophy (PhD)
  • Study mode: Full-time or part-time, in person
  • Year of entry: 2027

Fees and Funding

Fees for entry in 2027 have not yet been set. For reference, fees for 2026 were:

  • UK students (per annum): Band A - £5,238; Band B - £7,700; Band C - £13,200; Band D - £21,200; Band E - £36,100
  • International students (per annum): Band A - £29,900; Band B - £32,400; Band C - £37,900; Band D - £45,900; Band E - £60,800

There are a range of scholarships, studentships and awards at university, faculty and department level to support both UK and overseas postgraduate researchers. Visit the funding page to search for scholarships, studentships and awards you may be eligible for.

Eligibility Criteria

  • Standard academic entry requirement: An upper second-class (2:1) honours degree in a discipline directly relevant to the PhD OR any upper-second class (2:1) honours degree and a Master's degree at merit in a discipline directly relevant to the PhD.
  • English language: IELTS 6.5 overall with a minimum of 6 in writing and listening, and 5.5 in all other sub-tests. TOEFL iBT: At least 4.5 overall with no subskill below 4.5. Pearson Test of English (PTE): At least 70 overall with no subtest below 59.
  • Other combinations of qualifications and research or work experience may also be considered.

Application Process

  1. Identify the specific research project, CDT or dual-award you'd like to apply for or determine your own research project and title.
  2. Contact the project supervisor and discuss your suitability.
  3. Browse funding you are eligible for and discuss with your supervisor.
  4. Apply online including: programme name, research project title, proposed supervisor's name, funding details, supporting statement, details of previous university-level study, and names and contact details of two referees.
  5. Interview is required for entry.

Required Documents

  • Supporting statement (1-2 pages)
  • Certificates and transcripts
  • CV
  • English language proof
  • Two academic referees

Important Notes

  • The PhD is a three and a half year (or seven year, if taken part-time) degree resulting in a substantial thesis.
  • Scholarships, studentships and awards are available at university, faculty and department level.
  • An interview is required for entry to this programme.
  • The University of Manchester is regulated by the Office for Students (OfS).

How to Apply

Submit your application through the official portal before the deadline: Rolling admissions - Contact department for deadlines. Read the eligibility requirements carefully and prepare all requested documents — early applications are strongly recommended for competitive awards.
